question: TypeScript: types vs interfaces, generics, narrowing, and utility types?

scenes.sub: Types are checked before the code runs, then erased.
scenes.say: TypeScript. Four topics come up again and again: type versus interface, generics, narrowing, and utility types.

scenes.head: Think of a shipping label
scenes.say: Think of a shipping label. The label describes the parcel: fragile, two kilos. The warehouse checks parcels against labels before they leave. That is the compile step. But the delivered box has no label on it. Types are erased, so nothing is checked at runtime. Data from an A P I can still be wrong.

scenes.head: type vs interface
scenes.say: For object shapes they are almost the same. An interface describes an object and can extend another. A type can name anything: a union, a tuple, an intersection. Only interfaces support declaration merging, where a second declaration adds fields. Rule of thumb: interface for public object shapes, type for unions and everything else. Be consistent.

scenes.head: Generics: types as parameters
scenes.say: A generic is a function with a type placeholder. T is a placeholder filled in at each call. Pass numbers, and T is number, so the result is number or undefined. Pass strings, T is string. One function, fully typed, no copy and paste. You can add a constraint: K extends keyof T means the key must really exist on the object.

scenes.head: Narrowing and utility types
scenes.say: Narrowing means the compiler tracks what a value can be. Give each shape a kind field. Inside the if, after you check the kind, T S knows it is a circle and lets you read r. After the return, it knows it is a square. Utility types reshape types for you: Partial makes every field optional, Pick keeps some fields, Omit drops some.

scenes.say: Likely follow-ups. Any versus unknown? Unknown forces a check before use, any turns checking off. Are types checked at runtime? No, they are erased, so validate external data. What is a discriminated union? A union with a shared literal field to narrow on. The common mistake: using as to silence errors instead of narrowing.

lines: Types are compile-time only. Validate data at the boundary.
interface for object shapes, type for unions. Generics keep code reusable and typed.
Narrow with checks. Avoid any and as.
